dm_choice_overload.definition: The state in which too many options make the choosing harder instead of easier.
dm_choice_overload.example: Too many profiles, and the choosing turned into work rather than pleasure.

gd_shared_account.definition: What two people agree happened, and what each of them remembers about it.
gd_shared_account.example: Their shared account of the shift was simple, and both of them could still say it.

gem_stress_reactivity.definition: How strongly and how fast a person reacts to pressure; a tempo, not a character.
gem_stress_reactivity.example: Her stress reactivity is high in meetings and low in front of a machine.

one_time_code.definition: The short number a bank sends to confirm a login or a payment. Anyone who holds it can complete the action.
one_time_code.example: I gave them the one-time code, and that was the moment the account was theirs.

slice.definition: To cut something into thin, flat pieces.
slice.example: I slice the banana and put it on top.

transactive_memory.definition: The shared system by which a group, or a person and a tool, divides the work of remembering who knows what.
